bib.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Negative Contrastive Learning for Dense Text Retrieval

question: Why does dense text retrieval underperform sparse retrieval, and can training with globally hard negatives from an asynchronously refreshed ANN index fix it?
hypothesis: Local in-batch negatives are uninformative (near-zero loss and gradient), so selecting hard negatives globally from the whole corpus with the model being trained will speed convergence and raise accuracy.
contributions: Theoretical analysis (variance reduction / importance sampling) showing local in-batch negatives give diminishing gradient norms in dense retrieval
ANCE: negatives drawn from top results of an asynchronously refreshed ANN index built from the model being trained
Experiments on TREC 2019 DL, Natural Questions, TriviaQA and a commercial search engine, plus gradient-norm analysis

method.summary: A BERT-Siamese (RoBERTa-base) dot-product retriever trained with NLL loss. After a BM25-negative warm-up, an Inferencer re-encodes the corpus with a recent checkpoint and rebuilds a Faiss index every 10k batches while the Trainer continues; each positive gets one negative sampled uniformly from the ANN top 200 (minus positives).
method.task: first-stage dense text retrieval (web search passages/documents, open-domain QA)

datasets.name: MS MARCO / TREC 2019 DL Track (passage and document)
datasets.size: passage-level labels for one million Bing queries; TREC DL document task has 43 evaluation queries
datasets.split: train and dev from MS MARCO; test labels from NIST assessors, top-10 pooling
datasets.source: Bajaj et al. 2016; Craswell et al. 2020
datasets.preprocessing: document: FirstP = first 512 tokens; MaxP = split into 512-token passages (maximum 4), scores max-pooled

datasets.name: Natural Questions (NQ)
datasets.split: exact settings of Karpukhin et al. (2020)

datasets.name: TriviaQA (TQA)
datasets.split: exact settings of Karpukhin et al. (2020)

datasets.name: Commercial search engine first-stage production data
datasets.size: corpora of 250 million and 8 billion documents

models.name: ANCE (BERT-Siamese, shared encoder for q and d)
models.architecture: RoBERTa-base encoder, 768x768 projection layer on last-layer [CLS], then layer norm; dot product similarity
models.init_from: RoBERTa base for TREC DL, after BM25-negative warm-up; DPR released checkpoints for OpenQA

models.name: Rand Neg, NCE Neg, BM25 Neg, BM25 + Rand Neg (DPR style) and BM25-warm-up variants
models.architecture: same BERT-Siamese, differing only in negative construction

other.note: released models, retrieval swapped from DPR to ANCE

training.objective: negative log likelihood over (q, d+, d-) with d- from ANN top-k (Eq. 13); also tried cosine with BCE/hinge
training.lr: 5e-6 for document and 1e-6 for passage retrieval
training.lr_schedule: linear warm-up and decay after 5000 steps
training.batch_size: batch size 8, gradient accumulation step 2 on 4 GPUs
training.epochs: converges in about 10 epochs; about 1-2 hours per ANCE epoch
training.hardware: 1:1 Trainer:Inferencer GPU allocation, 4 GPUs for training; efficiency measured on a single 32GB V100, Intel Xeon Platinum 8168, 650GB RAM
training.compute: corpus re-encoding 10h per refresh for TREC DL documents (Table 5)

other.negative_sampling: one negative per positive, uniformly from ANN top 200
other.warm_up: BM25 negatives from MARCO official for TREC DL; released DPR checkpoints for OpenQA
other.tuned_configs: Table 7 lists the only hyperparameter explorations (lr 2e-7 to 1e-5, top-K 100 to 1000, refresh 5k to 20k)

inference.samples: not stated; single runs, no seeds reported
inference.retrieval: dot-product ANN search; OpenQA: top 20 passages to RAG-Token on NQ, top 100 to DPR BERT Reader on TQA

metrics.name: MRR@10
metrics.definition: mean reciprocal rank of first relevant result in top 10, MARCO Dev passage

metrics.name: NDCG@10
metrics.definition: TREC DL passage and document, official NIST labels

metrics.name: Recall@1k / Recall@100
metrics.definition: recall at cutoff; paper says recall on TREC DL is less meaningful due to low label coverage (high hole rate)

metrics.name: Coverage@20/100
metrics.definition: whether the top-20/100 retrieved passages include the answer

metrics.name: Hole@10
metrics.definition: fraction of top K ranked results without TREC labels

metrics.name: OpenQA test score
metrics.definition: end-to-end answer accuracy with fixed reader

metrics.name: Latency
metrics.definition: online, one query and 100 retrieved documents

baselines: BM25 -> Rand / NCE Neg / BM25 + Rand
eval.protocol: single runs reported; no seeds or significance tests stated; hyperparameters chosen by training loss curve and otherwise MARCO Dev loss

availability.data: public benchmarks; production data not released

limits: The gradient-norm bound is from Katharopoulos & Fleuret (2018) for MLPs and is carried over to BERT by assumption; the paper supports it with gradient-norm plots only.
The analysis uses a rough probability p = b|D-*|/|C|^2 for in-batch negatives without a derivation shown.
Hyperparameter exploration was barely done; Table 7 lists about all of it, chosen by training loss and MARCO Dev loss.
TREC DL 2019 pooled labels came only from sparse-retrieval systems, so DR has high hole rates and recall is not very informative.
No false-negative handling is discussed: ANCE samples from top 200 minus known positives, so unlabeled relevant documents may be used as negatives.
Single runs, no seeds or significance tests reported.
Commercial search gains (Table 3) are relative, on proprietary data and an unnamed metric.
RAG-Sequence was not used because the huggingface release was not stable; TriviaQA uses DPR Reader because RAG only released NQ models.
Training cost: each refresh re-encodes the corpus (10h for the TREC DL document corpus on one V100).

terms.definition: Approximate nearest neighbor Negative Contrastive Estimation: negatives are D-_ANCE = ANN_f(q,d) minus D+, the top results of the current model from an ANN index of the whole corpus
